name: building to the west

attributes.attribute: thrown at the youth while he slept

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: In traditional Celtic countries, building an addition on the west side of a house was unwise. Such a site could be fairy property. Buildings placed on gentle land, where fairies lived, drew endless trouble. A youth once built a cowhouse on such a place. He acted to spite the older people who had warned him. His cattle then began to die for no clear reason. Fairy darts were thrown at him while he slept in his bed. He removed the roof of the cowhouse to expose it to the weather. After that all was well again.

okr.objective: Convey the mythic theme that building to the west risked fairy land and brought trouble.
key_results: A west-side addition could be built on fairy property.
Buildings on gentle land where fairies lived drew endless trouble.
A youth built a cowhouse to spite older folk, and his cattle began to die.
